title: Landfall and Trail
premise: Salvage diver Petra Halloran raises a sealed chest from a wrecked river steamer, marked with the seal of a nation that no longer exists. The navy that sank the steamer decades ago recruits him — with quiet threats — to guide a covert expedition upriver to a glacier-bound valley before the calving season opens and then seals the route. Along the way he falls for expedition cartographer Ines Varga, who is secretly hunting the truth about her grandfather, a sailor aboard the sunken steamer. Petra must choose between loyalty to the navy that owns his silence and the truth Ines deserves, and in the end he opens the chest, publishes the expedition's findings, and brings his crew home alive just as the glacier closes the route behind them.
about_author: Edmund Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent a decade running salvage contracts along cold northern rivers before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels in which landscapes are adversaries and every moral choice has a current pulling against it.

chapters.title: The River Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Dredging a sanctioned wreck site, Petra recovers a lead-sealed chest bearing the crest of a vanished republic — and a navy launch appears within the hour to claim it. The emotional beat is the chill of recognition: he has measured his life in miles, and the river just measured it in consequences.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In a naval office smelling of brass and old paper, Commander Ashe offers a contract: guide a covert survey expedition upriver before calving season, or lose his salvage license and his freedom. Petra signs, telling himself it's just another paid run. The beat is uneasy self-deception.

chapters.title: A Cartographer with Questions
chapters.summary: Ines Varga's POV. Ines joins the expedition officially to map the upper river, unofficially to trace her grandfather, a steamer sailor listed as lost. She notices Petra flinch at the chest's seal and begins probing. The beat is wary curiosity sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Upriver, Against the Calendar
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The expedition fights rapids, rotting portages, and a dwindling window before the glacier route opens. Ashe's men grow secretive; a crewman who peeked into the chest is quietly reassigned. Petra realizes he isn't guiding an expedition — he's escorting a cover-up. The beat is mounting dread.

chapters.title: What the Steamer Carried
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines decodes her grandfather's salvaged letters: the steamer wasn't carrying refugees as history claims, but evidence of a massacre the navy committed and the drowned nation never sanctioned. She confronts Petra at night on the deck. The beat is the collision of her need for truth with his contract of silence.

chapters.title: The Valley Before the Ice
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The route opens — forty-eight hours of passable trail along the calving glacier. The team reaches the drowned nation's abandoned valley settlement and finds the massacre's physical proof preserved in ice. Ashe orders it documented, then sealed, forever. The beat is awe curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Broken Compass
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines secretly copies the evidence and photographs the ice-preserved records. Petra catches her — and instead of reporting her, helps her hide the copies, crossing his own line. A navy watcher sees them. The beat is love and truth fusing into open mutiny.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Ashe moves to detain Ines and seize the copies; Petra engineers a diversion, splitting the team and running the river early through untested rapids to outrun the navy launch. A crewman loyal to Ashe drowns, and Petra carries the weight of it. The beat is desperate, costly flight.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. At the river's mouth, Petra forces the confrontation: he opens the chest before naval officers, journalists, and the surviving crew, reading the massacre record aloud as the glacier route closes behind them, making concealment pointless. Ines stands witness beside him. The beat is truth detonating in public.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, resolution. Petra faces a tribunal that, swayed by public outrage, declines to prosecute him but ends his salvage career. He and Ines publish the full account, and on the riverbank where it began he stops measuring life in miles and starts measuring it in years — with her. The beat is hard-won peace.
